candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Artifact-grounded self-review closure: severe self-identified contradictions become blocking corrective obligations, not advisory prose
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: AutoResearchEval runs 8 harness-model combinations over the same 100 frontier-science tasks, producing 800 full trajectories, 73k tool calls and 12,712 process-level failure attributions. Three experts induced 45 failure patterns; the released methodology reports expert consensus kappa 0.85 after five rounds. Artifact-aware trajectory judging reaches kappa 0.75 at pattern level and 0.83 at root-cause level against expert annotation, versus 0.53/0.62 for a single-call transcript-only judge. Across all 12,712 hits, grounding/faithfulness, cognitive depth/adaptability and scientific integrity account for 92.1%; engineering robustness only 7.9%. The most frequent pattern, F.4 Uncorrected Self-Awareness, occurs in 82.5% of analyses: agents identify a severe flaw during their own review and ship anyway. The authors explicitly do not test an orchestration intervention.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: A useful control target is not more self-critique text but closure semantics: every severe review finding must link to the exact contradicting artifact, then transition to one of resolve-by-reexecution, reopen-plan/hypothesis, qualify/withhold-claim, or hard block. The artifact-aware judge result suggests transcript-only reflection misses precisely the evidence needed to enforce this transition.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Failure-diagnosis-derived mechanism hypothesis, not an intervention ablation. 100 tasks across seven domains and eight harness-model combinations support prevalence/general recurrence; they do not establish that this particular closure controller fixes the failures.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Turn-level credit redistribution for stable long-horizon RL of research agents
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Faraday trains a 27B research agent on Replica using modified GRPO. Its reward is averaged over three rubric-judge samples, and the judge assigns per-turn weights that rescale token advantages without changing total reward magnitude. In Appendix B's direct ablation, removing turn-level credit assignment from a late training checkpoint makes carry-forward mean reward collapse after about 50 steps; token entropy spikes then collapses, while Jensen-Shannon divergence between generation and training policies begins rising and eventually grows by roughly two orders of magnitude. With credit assignment retained, carry-forward reward rises steadily in the matched continuation.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: For long-horizon scientist-agent post-training, a single terminal reward should not be broadcast uniformly over all tokens. Evidence-attributed turn-level credit can stabilize optimization and may help train research policies where useful causal actions are sparse within long trajectories.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Direct training-stability ablation in one Faraday/Replica RL setup. It establishes a stability mechanism more strongly than a universal science-quality effect; exact attribution quality is still produced by the same learned rubric judge.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Researcher-coder hierarchy: train the scientific controller to delegate implementation to a strong coding tool instead of collapsing research and coding into one policy
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Faraday uses coding agents as tools. Appendix B trains the same Qwen3.6-27B base from scratch with matched tailpatch hyperparameters but without access to the coding-agent tool ('Faraday Coder'). That variant performs consistently worse at equal training steps before collapsing after roughly 300 steps. During the pre-collapse period it has twice Faraday's time horizon (60 versus 30 minutes) yet remains weaker. A separate generalization check swaps a partially trained Faraday from its train-time GPT-5.4-mini coding tool to GPT-5.5 and improves held-out AI-for-science replication scores without retraining the researcher policy.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Separate scientific control from code-production capacity: the researcher decides what experiment/reproduction to perform and delegates implementation to a replaceable stronger coder. This can raise the controller's effective capability ceiling and lets tool improvements transfer without retraining the scientific policy.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Direct within-lineage evidence on Replica paper-replication tasks, not open-ended novel discovery. The no-tool variant may differ in optimization dynamics beyond delegation itself, and the coding tool is a powerful frontier model, so compute/capability accounting should include it.

evidence_refinements: Candidate 022 is now implementation-confirmed: curate.py's confirmation rerun rematerializes the exact kept generator and calls the same evaluate_candidate path on disjoint seeds; scorer.py explicitly documents the historical API-error masquerading-as-model-failure bug and now carries api_error/api_error_rate; validate.py adds glyph_clean because the prior text/code gates structurally missed rendering substitution glyphs. This makes the shared-failure-channel interpretation stronger than a prose-only correction narrative.

Faraday's reward-judge human alignment should be described narrowly. Two rubric-judge draws have Kendall tau 0.66 versus 0.46 for baseline-judge draws and 0.30 between two humans, but rubric-judge versus human tau is only 0.19 versus 0.15 for the baseline. On disputed pairs humans side with the rubric judge 63% of the time, p=0.109, not statistically significant. The separate agent-comparison study deliberately selects tasks where the rubric judge puts Faraday >=0.2 above both baselines, so it supports only conditional agreement when the judge reports a clear Faraday advantage, not average human superiority over Claude/Codex.

Faraday nevertheless provides held-out task evidence: all agents receive the same materials and 60-minute single-GPU budget; Faraday is reported ahead of Claude and Codex on 60% of held-out AI-for-science tasks and by 6% and 8% average rubric score respectively. Treat these as rubric-judge results with the human-alignment caveat above.
negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: AutoResearchEval's authors locate the recurring deficit at a missing metacognitive loop, but they explicitly do not test whether an orchestration-level intervention closes it; candidate 027 is therefore a mechanism proposal grounded in prevalence, not a demonstrated fix.

Artifact-aware judging substantially improves agreement versus transcript-only judging in AutoResearchEval, but the judge itself is a fresh Claude Code session and can share model-family biases with evaluated systems; kappa is calibration to expert labels, not proof of scientific truth.

Faraday's task-specific rubric judge is lower-noise than its constant-prompt baseline, but human agreement is modest and disputed-pair preference is not statistically significant; do not use the judge as an independently validated scientific oracle.

Faraday's researcher-coder result should count the coding agent as part of the system's effective compute/capability. A small controller outperforming a coding baseline is not evidence that the small model alone contains superior scientific capability.

Replication post-training may teach transferable research process, but Replica remains paper replication with redacted figures and a rubric judge; transfer to genuinely novel discovery is not established.
frontier_additions: Inspect AutoResearchEval released 800-trajectory annotations to quantify which F.4 self-identified flaws were objectively repairable and whether later tool actions ever corrected them; derive a severity-to-action transition table without using downstream state.
Search for a matched intervention that converts self-review findings into mandatory re-plan/re-execute gates and measures end scientific outcome, to test candidate 027 causally.
Inspect Faraday Appendix B figure/raw training logs if public artifacts exist; recover numeric reward curves and exact matched checkpoint/seed details for credit-assignment and coder-tool ablations.

Search independent long-horizon RL evidence for learned turn-level credit assignment in research/scientific agents, especially where credit is verified against artifacts rather than generated by the same reward model.
Test whether researcher-coder hierarchy persists with matched total inference compute and a weaker/stronger coder sweep rather than one no-tool ablation.
Inspect Replica innovation-task variants and human study carefully before claiming replication training transfers to discovery-like changed-claim/dataset tasks.

For candidate 022, inspect tests around api_error_rate and glyph_clean and seek an independent project where orthogonal validation paths actually prevent a promotion error rather than only catch it post hoc.
